FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Woodworking Hand Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production 
Engineering Division Council. 

Carpenter's bevels are primarily used for testing and checking trueness of an angle or flatness or/ 
and squareness of surfaces by placing it at right angles to adjacent surfaces and observing if light 
shows between the work-piece and the bevel. 

While formulating this standard, assistance has been taken from BS 3322 : 1980 'Carpenter's 
squares and bevels, issued by British Standards Institution ( BSI ). 



IS 13345 : 1992 



Indian Standard 



CARPENTER'S BEVELS — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

l.l This standard covers the requirements of 
carpenter's bevel. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard :

4.1 The dimensions of carpenter's bevel shall 
be as given in Table 1.

5.1 The blades shall be manufactured from 
suitable steels meeting the requirements given 
in 5 and 8.

5.2 The rivets shall be manufactured from mild 
steel wire conforming to IS 280 : 1978 or brass 
conforming to IS 319 : 1974. 

5.3 The face plate shall be made from brass 
conforming to IS 319 : 1974. The stock shall be 
manufactured from any good quality seasoned 
wood, such as ebony ( Diospyros sp, ) or rose- 
wood ( Dalbergia latifolia Roxb. ) and shall be 
free from deleterious defects ard shall be straight 
grained. The timber shall be free from sapwood, 
decay ( rot ), insect holes, pith knots, checks, 
splits, warp, wanes and other defects. 

5.3>1 Alternatively the stock may be made from 
malleable cast iron or suitable plastics. 

6 HARDNESS 

6.1 The blade of the carpenter's bevel shall be 
hardened and tempered to achieve hardness in 
the range of 418 HV to 460 HV, 

7 MANUFACTURE, WORKMANSHIP AND 
FINISH 

7.1 Manufacture and Workmanship 

7.1.1 All working faces and edges of the bevels 
together with components shall be smoothly 
finished. When plates, tips and spacers are 
used they shall be smoothly finished and flush 
with adjacent surfaces. 

7.1.2 Facing plates on wooden stocks shall be 
positively secured to the stock. 

7.1.3 Tips and the spacers on the stock for 
the bevels shall be positively secured to the 
stock. 

7.1.4 Means shall be provided for positively 
locking the bevel blade in any position. The 
major diameter of the screw used for the pur- 
pose shall be not less than that for M5 screw 
thread. The locking screw shall not protrude 
beyond the stock working face on at least one 
side. 

7.2 Finish 

7.2.1 Blades 

The blades shall be smoothly finished and shall 
be chemically blued or blackened or suitably 
protected. 

7.2.2 Stocks 

The stocks shall be smoothly finished and if 
made of wood shall be varnished/polished. 



7.2.3 Other Metal Parts 

Other metal parts shall 
anti-corrosion treatment. 

8 ACCURACY 



be given a suitable 



8.1 Straightness of Working Faces ( Inner and 
Outer ) and Working Edges 

The difference between the highest and lowest 
points of the stock working edge shall not 
exceed 0'25 mm. The difference between th^ 
highest and lowest points of the blade working 
edge shall not exceed 0'125 mm. A typical 
method of test given in Annex A-1. 

8.2 Parallelism of Working Faces and Working 
Edges 

The maximum error in parallelism between the 
stock working edge shall not exceed 0'38 mm 
and the blade working edges shall not exceed 
0*18 mm. A typical method of test is given in 
Annex A-2. 

9 PERFORMANCE TEST 

9.1 Permanent Set 

Secure the stock firmly and flex the tip of the 
blade through an angle of 15° in either lateral 
direction for all other sizes of bevels. The blade' 
of each bevel shall be fully extended and in line 
with the stock when conducting this test. No 
permanent set shall result on bevel blade. 

9.2 Blade Security 

Lock the blade in the fully extended position 
and at 90° to the stack. Secure the stock 
firmly and apply a load of I'S kg to the tdgQ of 
the blade to give a turning moment of 1*5 Nm 
about the axis of the locking screw. Locking 
of the screw shall be verified after the removal 
of the load {see Fig. 1). The blade shall 
remain at 90*" to the stock. 

10 DESIGNATION 

10.1 The carpenter's bevel shall be designated 
by the commonly used name, nominal size and 
number of this Indian Standard. 

Example: A Carpenter's bevel of nomial size 
190 mm shall be designated as : 
Carpenter's bevel —190— IS 13345 

11 MARKING 

11.1 The carpenter's bevels shall be legibly 
marked with the manufacturer's name or trade- 
mark and the nominal size. 



!S 13345 ; 1992 




Fig. 1 Blade Security 



ANNEX A 
( Clauses S A and 82) 

METHOD OF TESTING ACCURACY 



A-1 CHECKING THE STRAIGHTNESS OF 
WOBKING FACES AND WORKING EDGES 

The working faces and working edges of the 
bevels can be tested for accuracy by bedding 
them evenly on the working surface of a grade B 
surface plate, confoiming to IS 3510 : 1966 and 
ensuring that a feeler guage conforming to 
IS 3179 : 1976 and with a thickness of the 



maximum tolerance as specified in 8.1.1 shall 
not pass between them and the surface plate. 

A-2 CHECKING THE PARALLELISM OF 
FACES AND OF WORKING EDGES 

The parallelism of the working edges of bevels 
as specified in 8,2«1 can be checked by direct 
measurement. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Burean of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of 
goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
